explanation: Baseline hypotheses worth revisiting: (1) the baseline ignored u3 entirely in its linear term, so a real u3 effect had to be absorbed by noise; adding an explicit u3 coefficient lets the fit use that signal. (2) The baseline applied a saturating rescale out -> clip(out/(1+|out|),-1,1)*(1+|out|), which is a non-identity nonlinear map that compresses large responses and can only hurt a linear-in-parameters least-squares fit; removing it preserves the linear structure the host fits. (3) The baseline used a cubic mixed term u0*u1*u2 which is collinear-ish with the pairwise terms at fit start; replacing it with a symmetric pairwise term c12*u1*u2 keeps a quadratic, well-conditioned basis. These are hypotheses about fit behavior, not verified improvements; the host's single evaluation under the frozen allocation is the only measurement, and it is limited to the train scope recorded in the baseline. Declared count rises from 7 to 8, still within the 0..16 contract, so the complexity-reduction branch of the objective is not pursued. No files, networks, subprocesses, extra packages, row indices, or lookup tables are used.
